newsitem.title: UK: Platinum metals steadier in London, gold quiet.
newsitem.headline: Platinum metals steadier in London, gold quiet.

text.p: A degree of normality returned to the platinum group metals (PGMs) markets on Wednesday as buying came in following lower prices the previous day, dealers said

Platinum and palladium were both firmer, fixing at $455.00 per ounce, up $3.00, and $218.00, up $6.00, repectively. Both were above their previous London closes, which had been influenced by selling in New York.

Gold fixed at $343.70, just five cents down on Tuesday afternoon, and dealers said little business had been seen in London since the opening. "There is not too much upside in gold just now," one dealer said.
But some others felt there was a chance of the metal building on its established support at $340.00.
Even so, a $346.00 resistance cap would take some shifting, according to technical analysts.
This week's weaker dollar and continuing doubts about European Monetary Union (EMU) start-up have lent only passive support to gold, dealers said.

The perception is that a delay to the proposed 1999 EMU start would reduce the likelihood of European central banks selling gold reserves to meet EMU entry criteria. In the longer term a delay could encourage "safe haven" buying of gold, analysts said.
Silver could have a more positive shorter-term price profile, dealers said. But even that was limited.
"(The price spike) last Friday definied the upper end of its range at $4.95 and that may have been spillover panic from the PGMs," a dealer said.
Silver was indicated at $4.77/$4.79, down a cent.
Dealers said the PGMs were more recognisably normal now that they had corrected from the highs of a week ago.
News from Tokyo that a Russian export official had said PGM exports to Japan would begin for 1997 as soon as possible had been factored into the price.
"The panic is dying down and dealers are trying to be responsible and keep the market trading," a dealer said.
But tight supply due to delayed Russian exports meant lease rates were still abnormally high, although off their peaks.
Leasing platinum for a month was quoted at 100 percent and palladium at 120 percent and the forward curve was reflecting more liquidity in forward months.
Platinum and palladium prices and lending rates have shot up this year due to adminstrative problems that have taken major supplier Russia out of the market since last December.
